titleStmt.title: Funerary inscription on the founders' tomb

support.p: Perhaps on the back wall of the (now blocked)arcosolium nichein the south wall of the narthex. According to Andreas Rhoby it may have originally been rendered in marble or other stone (perhaps a part of the sarcophagus not visible to modern viewers?)

handDesc.handNote: The 19th-century painted inscription that reproduces the text is in cursive minuscule script with accents and breathings. There is no evidence regarding the script of the original Byzantine inscription. letter-heights

origin.origPlace: Vatopedi, Chapel of Saint Nicholas (south of the main church)

history.provenance: Modern location(s) (if different from repository, above)

lg.l: μονῆς καλύπτει τῆσδε, ὦ φίλε ξένε.

div.p: The text is reproduced in the painted inscription on the wall blocking the arcosolium niche. This inscription was probably painted in the early 19th century. The 19th-century inscription is edited by Theocharis Pazaras, whereas the philological edition provided here follows the edition by Andreas Rhoby. We prefer the latter, since the original Byzantine version is assumed to be lost and we treat the text as a reconstruction. A. Rhoby has corrected line 4 of the 19th-century copy from ἀγαποίσας to ἀγαπούσας.
